findings.reason: a node implementing §2 as written ships a command whose own declared defect is live, and no done-when test would catch it; the plan needs a work item (distinct replacement job name, or name-independent cancel) plus its test.
findings.text: §2 lists defect 2 ("Two copies of one profile carry the same job name. So `agent shutdown` would cancel both.") as a blocker to a safe overlap, but none of the three work items or four done-when bullets addresses it: the overlap still submits the replacement under the profile slug name, and `shutdown` (cli.py:1117) cancels every job whose `%j` equals the resolved slug, so a coordinator running `agent shutdown <slug>` during the overlap window cancels both the old and the new engine

findings.reason: without the arming path the hold is a race an implementer would resolve arbitrarily, and a hold lost to the job's own write routes traffic to an ungenerated engine, defeating the section's whole mechanism.
findings.text: §2 says the replacement is submitted "with its registration held" and that the hold marker is "written and removed by imas_ambix/agent/registry.py", but the serve registration is written by the *generated batch script* inside the new job (slurm.py's `registry write` step, run before the readiness loop), while §1 line 52 says the script is generated "as today" — the plan names no path by which the submit-time hold reaches that job's own registry write (a `--hold` on `registry write`, or a hold keyed by job id that the job's write preserves), and a hold written by `restart` after `sbatch` can be cleared by the job's later write

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified: `restart` (cli.py:2239), `_running_jobs` (:1219, operator-scoped `-u`), `_probe_endpoint` (:1307), `_resolve_router_upstreams` (:1507, with the registration path and the `_discover_live_routes` scheduler-only path both present), the registry-write step in the generated serve script (slurm script writes registration before the readiness loop), `RealMemory`/`AllocMem`/`CfgTRES`/`AllocTRES` all present on `scontrol show node 98dci4-gpu-0003`, AGENTS.md §2 (core ledger), §3b (2026-09-07 zero-downtime rotation), and ops/lane-cycle/AGENTS.md step 7 "Record the cycle" all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each section names a runnable pytest command and a negative control (§1 deletes the `finally` resume, so its exception-path test fails; §2 removes the hold skip on the registration path and on the scheduler-only path, each failing its own test).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the cycle's durable record is `lane-cycles.jsonl` beside `lane.json`, and the gates run in place on the fleet node; no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the proposed symbols (`reload.py`, `--mode`, `held_registry` marker, `lane-cycles.jsonl`) carry no ticket numbers, stage names or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's changed room-check paragraph is sound (its motivating evidence checks out: the two `murawan` embedding jobs each carry `gres/gpu=1` in `scontrol show job`, which `_running_jobs` cannot see), but §2 declares a second defect it never resolves, and it does not name how the hold is armed before the job writes its own registration.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 is the paused-cycle command, §2 the overlap mode, §3 the deferred router handover; each carries one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §1 and §2 cross-link via data-links (`hot-reload-the-serve#s2` / `#s1`), the §1-then-§2 build order is declared in followup f-hrs-001, and `plan-after` local-lane-admission-control resolves to docs/plans/local-lane-admission-control.html.
